articleTitle: Enhancing Supply Chain Performance through Production Planning: A Model for Moroccan Aerospace Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article introduces a conceptual model aimed at evaluating the influence of production planning on supply chain logistics performance, specifically within the commercial domain of Moroccan aerospace companies. Through an empirical investigation involving a survey distributed to 41 professionals in aeronautical logistics, purchasing, planning, and related fields, we used latent variable structural modeling with the partial least squares (PLS) approach and XL-STAT software (version 2021). This research paper assesses the reliability and validity of the suggested model, ultimately affirming that production planning significantly impacts supply chain logistics performance. The findings provide insights for potential enhancements and actionable plans for strategic and tactical decision-making within the logistics department.

articleTitle: Quantitative analysis of the main causes of road insecurity around schools in the city of Sousse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article explores the problem of road insecurity around primary schools in the governorate of Sousse in Tunisia. This research focused on 377 students aimed to assess their knowledge of road safety and their home-school travel habits and focused on 377 parents in order to collect data on knowledge, beliefs and perceptions regarding road safety in school perimeter. And on the basis of 23 selected schools, the availability of road safety devices around the schools was assessed. The study examines factors contributing to this insecurity, including infrastructure design, road signs, driver behaviors, and student transportation practices. The results indicate that 83% of the students surveyed are not aware of road safety. 43.7% of parents of students who use walking as a means of transport declared that the path, they took seemed dangerous. Most schools do not have all the means of safety for students. Proposed solutions include improvements to road infrastructure, targeted awareness campaigns for parents and students, as well as initiatives to promote safer modes of transportation for students. The study offers important insights for policymakers, urban planners and road safety professionals, aiming to create safe and supportive environments for student travel.

articleTitle: Improvement of the supplier selection process in the Automotive Industry: Case study with a Moroccan Tier 1 Company
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The automotive industry's supply chain management is undergoing a challenging phase due to the transition from fuel to electrification. This shift is significantly impacting three key aspects: sustainability, resilience, and green behavior. As the supplier selection process (SSP) is an interesting field in the automotive supply chain, this paper aims to explain the interest that companies are giving to the supplier selection problem according to a literature review of the most important cited articles in the last decade. The paper identifies the most important criteria for supplier evaluation and selection by examining the key steps that constitute the SSP. Furthermore, the paper incorporates a case study detailing the SSP employed by a Moroccan company operating as a tier 1 supplier to different Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) in the automotive sector.

articleTitle: Diagnosis and quantification of heating and cooling energy needs of a residential home in Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: These investigations aim to diagnose and measure the energy usage of a genuine residential building in the Mediterranean environment at the Tlemcen site. The method being used is based on an integrative approach to evaluate the energy performance of heating and cooling, domestic hot water production, free and internal loads connected to lighting, and equipment and occupants are not taken into account. Weather statistics are used to determine the yearly needs for heating and cooling using climatic data from 2020. To ascertain the appropriate energy cost, a technical and economic study would be of interest to us. Living in this apartment complex is therefore not affordable. The primary causes of heat loss in buildings are the ground, roof, and facade walls (more than 70% of total losses). In order to construct ecologically and bioclimatically friendly homes that fit the climate of the area, the evaluation functioned as a fundamental survey. To increase the building's energy efficiency, passive and active design elements must be integrated.

articleTitle: Mediating the role of Internet of Things in Sustainable Automotive Supply Chain: Practical Evidence from a Delphi Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Businesses are implementing environmentally conscious practices in response to the significant environmental challenges that humanity will face over the next decade. In order to develop an environment-based perspective, in this study, a sustainable automotive supply chain (SASC) is integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) technology and offers concrete steps toward a more prosperous ecological future. Based on 29 factors that represent the rectifications of four stakeholders, the research provides a theoretical framework for evaluating SASC operations in the ReSOLVE model using IoT. The framework was then verified using two exhaustive rounds of a Delphi study that involved professionals from the IoT, SASC, and sustainability domains. The findings indicate that companies could enhance the connectivity among the primary IoT tools in SASC by utilizing the proposed conceptual environmental framework. This would facilitate the formulation of cohesive strategies aimed at fostering sustainable growth. This study makes a substantial contribution to the body of knowledge regarding the sustainability and digitalization of the SASC, especially in light of the severe pressure, heightened competition, and unpredictability that the SASC faces.

articleTitle: Contribution of Geomatic in the improvement of road traffic in Algeria (Oran)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This research aims to investigate and analyze different Road Traffic Accidents (RTAs) and conflicts. An approach that includes all the necessary information about crashes is thus set up in a geographical information system (GIS) according to several different characteristics. As a result, incorporating the Severity Index (SI) into the identification of Road Traffic Accident (RTA) hotspots provides a more nuanced understanding, enabling traffic authorities to comprehensively grasp the root causes of each incident. This groundbreaking study not only stands as the inaugural initiative of its kind in Algeria but also holds considerable potential to substantially contribute to addressing similar issues not just in Oran but across various cities.

articleTitle: Procurement Improvement Process Based on Industry 4.0 & Lean Manufacturing: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The procurement can be considered as the most crucial process in supply chain management, it absorbs all requests of customers demand, especially for automotive industry, which know fluctuation in demand every day and every period. But how companies can ensure the raw material with the constraint of supplying? and how the application of industry 4.0 can improve this process? This paper's goal is to investigate an example for an automotive Japanese company, we will first display a short evaluation of the literature regarding SCM; Industry 4.0, RFID… Then we will present a case study for the implementation of supply chain management to Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Reverse logistics: research background and topic trends
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Actually, reverse logistics has turned into a focal point of interest for the majority research centers focuses, as it offers an answer for accomplishing a harmony among benefit and regard for the environment. Its guideline is the formation of financial value, appeared in the re-utilization of items toward the finish of their useful life, and ecological value, appeared in the minimization of the utilization of non-renewable natural resources as well as decreasing the negative natural effects of production. This economic environmental combination that organizations should accomplish, is forced from competitivity and administrative regulations. The objective of this paper is to make an examination of workmanship to sum up the level at which science has managed reverse logistics. For this, we had gathered 132 papers distributed between 2015 to 2023 that treat profoundly reverse logistics, and that use various devices and new innovations. Our examination separates topics treated in three clusters to review what was dealt with and find the gap of the literature about reverse logistics. The objective of our review is to give a worldwide outline about reverse logistics.

articleTitle: Driving Green Innovation: The Nexus of Green Intellectual Capital and Supply Chain Integration: A Comprehensive Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: With growing concern about environmental issues all over the world, companies are pressured to rethink their operations and maintain sustainable practices. At the heart of this change, we find the concept of green innovation, which aims to balance economic developpement and sustainability.Two key concepts are at the heart of Green Innovation: Green Intellectual Capital (GIC) and Green Supply Chain Integration (GSCI).Green Intellectual Capital includes the knowledge as well as the essential skills for sustainable development. Likewise, Green Supply Chain Integration (GSCI) engages collaboration across the supply chain to effectively manage environmental practices. Synergy between the GIC and the GSCI is essential. We assume that green intellectual capital is a catalyst for green supply chain integration, which in turn ensures transparent internal and external collaboration to promote not only sustainable development but also aligns business processes with environmental principles, thereby enhancing green innovation capabilities.The interaction between (GIC) and (GSCI) is examined in this paper, shedding light on their combined impact in promoting green innovation.

articleTitle: Sustainable Supply Chain Management in Morocco: A Critical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This paper provides a critical analysis of sustainable supply chain management (SSCM) in Morocco, focusing on the integration of technological innovation and policy reforms in an emerging economy context. Drawing from a range of recent scholarly works, this study explores Morocco’s adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies, blockchain implementation, and strategic policy initiatives. Key findings highlight Morocco’s commitment to enhancing operational efficiency and environmental sustainability, as well as the need for stronger vertical linkages and enhanced policy frameworks in supply chain management. The research reveals Morocco’s multifaceted approach to SSCM, marked by advancements in technology and challenges in implementation. This study contributes to the broader discourse on sustainable supply chain management, offering insights into Morocco’s strategies and innovations, with implications for other emerging economies. The paper concludes that ongoing collaboration and innovation are essential for further enhancing the sustainability of Morocco’s supply chains.

articleTitle: The Artificial Intelligence and Public Procurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Public procurement is an essential part of the economy [1], the public procurement process contains several steeps, from the expression of the need to the final execution of the contracts (Works, studies or services), in each steep there is some repetitive tasks, made by the purchaser, and data generated by the process (Technical, administrative and financial data, related to the documents of bidders, and necessary for the completion of the procurement act).The objective of this paper is to carry out a literature review, to identify the various research that have addressed the subject of the contribution of Artificial Intelligence for public procurement, and to highlight the field of public procurement, where Artificial Intelligence could be used, such analyzing data generated in the process, fighting corruption, and enhancing the efficiency of public procurement, as detailed in this paper.

articleTitle: Quantitative Study of Electricity Consumption: Regression on the Main Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Electricity management is a comprehensive field within environmental science that involves the regulation, oversight, and preservation of energy. It contributes greatly to improve the standard of living of every individual in different levels. This study seeks to determine the factors that affect electricity consumption in the residential sector of Tunisia. To achieve this goal and address the issue of multicollinearity among the explanatory variables, we chose principal component regression (PCR) as our regression model. The effectiveness of this PCR model will be validated through its application to a regional dataset, which was previously analyzed with initially correlated variables.

articleTitle: Green supplier selection criteria in automotive industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to carefully choose and evaluate the green selection criteria that are applied by automobile sector enterprises when choosing their suppliers. We suggest utilizing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) for data analysis in our hybrid multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approach. The first stage was to identify green selection criteria for suppliers, a procedure that was guided by the body of existing literature. Subsequently, the opinions of five experts were gathered to evaluate the significance of these green criteria in alignment with the objectives of the automotive industry. Using the AHP methodology, weights were assigned to these criteria. Notably, “Sustainable Product Design” received the highest weight (0.164), followed by “Health and Security” (0.153), "ISO 14001 Certification" (0.129), “Green Packaging” (0.105), and “Investment Recovery” (0.094). These five criteria carry the greatest weight, underscoring their paramount importance in future research for the evaluation of green criteria in supplier selection within the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Green purchasing Logistics: A lever for Ecological Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: In light of the increasing awareness of environmental issues and the absence of an evaluation methodology for ecological purchasing logistics, supply chains are confronted with a major challenge in transitioning to ecological purchasing practices. This paper proposes a new ecological purchasing process that incorporates the environmental dimension. Additionally, it introduces a methodology for evaluating the ecological performance of purchasing logistics by suggesting new composite performance indicators. This evaluation is conducted using a multi-criteria analysis method that enables the identification of the causes of underperformance in ecological purchasing logistics.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of biodiesel on the energy transition in the transport sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Transportation plays a key role in air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. These emissions are at the root of climate change, air quality degradation and other environmental problems. Promoting the utilization of renewable energies and decreasing reliance on fossil fuels is crucial in minimizing the environmental repercussions of transportation. This study aims to investigate the relationship between biofuel and transportation as a green energy capable of limiting the amount of greenhouse gas emissions caused by petroleum gasoline in US. Utilizing renewable energies in transportation reduces greenhouse gas emissions and atmospheric pollutants, enhancing air quality and lessening reliance on imported fossil fuels.

articleTitle: Energy optimization approach for the Single-Row Facility Layout Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This study delves into the critical realm of facility layout optimization, focusing on minimizing costs associated with interactions between facilities. It extends this optimization to reduce energy consumption (EC) during material movements, crucial for environmental protection and sustainable development. The Single-Row Facility Layout Problem (SRFLP) is explored as a specialized instance of the Facility Layout Problem (FLP), with applications across industries like manufacturing, hospitals, and supermarkets. The study employs a Quadratic Assignment Problem (QAP) to model the SRFLP, incorporating EC and position constraints. Through practical examples and the use of the CPLEX Studio IDE 22.1.1 solver, the research demonstrates the effectiveness of the mathematical model in optimizing facility layouts to minimize handling cost and EC. The article contributes to advancing mathematical modeling techniques for facility layout optimization and showcases practical applications in real-world scenarios, emphasizing the importance of energy-efficient facility arrangements for operational efficiency and sustainability.

articleTitle: Towards Proactive Maintenance : The Implementation of Digitized SCADA Systems for Predictive Maintenance Optimization in Production Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This paper advocates for the adoption of predictive maintenance strategies in production companies, highlighting the transition from traditional reactive and preventive maintenance approaches. It emphasizes the importance of data acquisition, management, and utilization in enabling predictive maintenance, proposing the development and implementation of a digitized Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. The proposed solution integrates advanced technologies such as sensors, Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and artificial intelligence (AI) to automate data acquisition, processing, and predictive analytics. Through systematic implementation, organizations can enhance operational efficiency, reduce downtime, and transition to proactive maintenance strategies. The paper presents the architecture, infrastructure setup, and testing methodology used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed system. Future research directions include continuous refinement of predictive models, scalability across industries, and understanding human factors for successful implementation.

articleTitle: Road insecurity: towards the development of a new proactive strategy in Tunisia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This study presents a new strategy for road safety focusing on accidents in Tunisia. Utilizing both univariate and multivariate descriptive analyses, the research aims to comprehensively understand the patterns and factors contributing to road accidents. Through univariate analysis, the study examines the evolution of accident rates and mortality, while multivariate analysis, such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), provides insights into the complex relationships between various variables related to road safety. By combining these analytical approaches, the study seeks to develop a proactive strategy that addresses the specific challenges of road safety in Tunisia, ultimately aiming to reduce accident rates and improve overall road safety conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Management: A Blockchain-Based Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The pharmaceutical supply chain is intricate, involving various stakeholders such as manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, pharmacies, regulatory bodies, and healthcare providers. This complexity introduces challenges, including a lack of transparency, counterfeit drugs, and limited access to crucial information. These challenges emphasize the critical need for the implementation of a robust tracking system that ensures security, privacy, transparency, decentralization, and authenticity across the entire supply chain. This study proposes a solution by introducing a blockchain-based model for pharmaceutical supply chain management. Capitalizing on the decentralized and transparent features inherent in blockchain technology, our model aims to effectively address the aforementioned challenges and elevate the overall efficiency and integrity of the pharmaceutical supply chain. This research significantly contributes to the integration of innovative technologies, such as blockchain, to mitigate risks and establish a safer and more reliable pharmaceutical supply chain.

articleTitle: Unveiling Medical Transportation Problems: extra-hospital, inter-hospital and intra-hospital challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to identify the main issues in the extra-hospital, intra-hospital and inter-hospital medical patient transportation. These problems have been determined at international scale. The methodology followed in this paper consists, firstly, on identifying the problems based on existing scientific articles in the literature. We then used quality management tools to classify the problems using a mind map for extra-hospital medical transport. Then, using a cause tree, the problems linked to intra-hospital medical transport were mapped and structured. Finally, an Ishikawa diagram was drawn up to group the problems of inter-hospital transport into families. The results showed that the three types of medical transport suffer from various organisational and technical problems.

articleTitle: Cryptocurrencies and Environmental Sustainability: A Complex Challenge and Emerging Positive Trends for Logistics Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The relationship between cryptocurrencies and energy consumption is complex, and raises concerns due to the carbon footprint associated with mining. Discussions and initiatives to make the industry more sustainable are underway, but there remains a challenge to reconcile cryptocurrency development with environmentally friendly practices. Supply chain logistics transactions face a challenge in adapting to the digitization of transactions using cryptocurrency. Through a coherence and co-movement study, we highlight a significant correlation between the Environmental Attention Index and the Cryptocurrency Market Index, testifying to a growing awareness of environmental issues among media players. Positive trends towards sustainability are also apparent, signalling a move towards more responsible practices aligned with contemporary environmental sustainability imperatives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Transparency and Efficiency: Leveraging Blockchain for Overcoming Challenges in Plastic Recycling Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The effective management of physical flows and information is a major challenge for PET plastic recycling companies. In this study, we propose a decision-making modeling approach to ensure traceability and reliability of data throughout the supply chain. Our system, using robust processes and appropriate technological infrastructure, allows for the collection, verification, and exchange of information related to PET plastic waste between various stakeholders. Using a combination of quantitative and qualitative techniques, we provide in-depth analysis of data to optimize business operations and avoid discrepancies between the quantities of waste delivered by suppliers and the quantities sold. Our study results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in controlling flows and ensuring data reliability, contributing to a more sustainable and responsible supply chain management in the PET plastic recycling industry.

articleTitle: The Impact of Traffic Lights and Electrification’s Fleet on Energy Consumption and Emissions : A Tunisian Intersections Case of Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This study investigates the importance of traffic control strategy in a Tunisian crossroads by highlighting the analogy between the influence of static traffic lights and the adaptive strategy upon road traffic performance. Also, it considers the importance of integrating battery electric vehicles and fuel cell vehicles for different levels of electrification to reduce many environmental and energetic impacts. This research tries to visualize the energy consumption and emissions generated when two control traffic lights operate for conventional, electric, and fuel-cell vehicles. Static and adaptive strategies and electric vehicles have been estimated using a microscopic traffic simulator SUMO (Simulation of Urban Mobility) combined with Python; it is worth noticing that adaptive strategy and electric vehicles are a significant solution in reducing energy consumption, environmental impacts, and queue length and in guaranteeing better road traffic system performance.

articleTitle: Supply Chain Management and Artificial Intelligence: A Bibliometric Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This paper study the connection between Supply Chain Management (SC Management) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) using bibliometric analysis. A total of 595 documents extracted from the Scopus database in the business and management fields were used to visualize keyword co-occurrence and to analyze citations related to authors, sources, documents, and countries. This review emphasizes the evolving prospect of SC Management and AI and their increasing importance in the academic world, and elucidates the various SC Management sub-fields and their relationship with AI and other digital technologies

articleTitle: An Improved population-based Simulated Annealing algorithm for solving a Green Vehicle Routing Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Within the realm of sustainable development, the Green Vehicle Routing Problem (GVRP) has attracted considerable attention due to its capacity to optimize routes to minimize emissions within third-party logistics. As an NP-hard combinatorial problem, the GVRP demands the utilization of various metaheuristic algorithms. Nevertheless, these algorithms are often crafted to handle continuous decision variables and necessitate adaptation to accommodate binary/integer variables. This investigation addresses the Emissions Vehicle Routing Problem (EVRP), an extension of the GVRP, with the objective of minimizing both distance traveled and carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) emissions. To this end, we propose an enhanced population-based simulated annealing (IPSA) algorithm. The IPSA is crafted by combining a novel technique for generating feasible neighboring real-valued solutions, thereby facilitating a profound exploration of the search space. Furthermore, we introduce a novel encoding/decoding methodology that translates a prospective realvalued solution into a viable integer-valued solution for the EVRP dilemma. Through exhaustive experimentation and comparative search across various EVRP instances, our findings evince the efficacy of the IPSA algorithm regarding to well-known metaheuristic algorithms. Our inquiry underscores the capacity of the IPSA algorithm to attain high-caliber EVRP solutions.

articleTitle: Lean Six Sigma in Higher Education: Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Higher education is a complex and dynamic field that aims to provide students with the knowledge, skills and experience needed to succeed in their careers. To meet the growing challenges of quality, efficiency and student satisfaction, some higher education institutions are adopting process improvement methodologies, such as Lean Six Sigma. The goal is to improve procedures, optimize resources and improve the student experience, which is essential to the overall success of the institution. The objective of this paper is to examine in depth 28 general literature articles on the LSS approach in the higher education sector, in order to provide a detailed analysis of its implementation. The results of this study were ranked according to the number of citations in articles dealing with the LSS approach in higher education institutions. Based on our assessment, we found that 70% of the case studies examined the implementation of LSS in the academic context of higher education, while 30% of the articles dealt with the use of this method to improve administrative procedures in this sector. Subsequently, we found that 8 critical success factors are essential to ensure the sustainability and success of LSS implementation, in order to benefit from the 6 main benefits of LSS implementation in the higher education sector.

articleTitle: Hybrid Transport mode selection using machine learning and MCDM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Urban transport users play a critical role in the success of public transportation systems as they are the primary consumers of these services. Understanding the characteristics and preferences of these users is essential to enhance the quality of public transport services and to meet the needs of diverse populations. The level of satisfaction with transport services among urban users can be influenced by various factors related to transport mode, including security, duration, punctuality, environmental impact, and cost. Even though the importance of these objective criteria, subjectivity in selecting the transport mode remains prominent especially when considering similar users' preferences. The study aims to propose a hybrid transport mode selection based on similar users' preferences and objective transport mode criteria in Sousse Region. Generated results proves a good performance of our system.

articleTitle: Transition to Supply chain 4.0 based on Risk Management and Inventive Design in a Circular Economy environment: State of the art
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Industry 4.0is not just a technological evolution; it's not just more intelligence in components, products or equipment. There's a whole philosophy behind it that's a real threat to Small and Medium-sized Enterprises integrating into this approach. It therefore, the risks attributable to the transition to the supply chain 4.0, becomes important to identify and analyze them. The objective is then to adopt innovative approaches and methods to boost the robustness and capability of the managerial systems, technologies, knowledge, etc. available to Small and Medium Enterprises ’ supply chain (SC), so that they are ready to counter the various obstacles that could impact the transition process. Through this study, we aim to help managers decide to integrate digital transformation by identifying and analyzing the risks involved in the transition to SC 4.0 in a Circular Economy environment.

articleTitle: Smart city implementation of electric vehicles: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Integrating Electric Vehicles (EVs) into smart cities (SCs) offers a great chance to decrease greenhouse gas emissions and improve urban areas in city logistics. Nevertheless, the integration of EVs into SCs entails notable dangers and obstacles that need thorough consideration. While several publications discuss the technical hurdles of integrating electric vehicles, they tend to overlook other significant issues that may come from this integration. This paper examines the potential hazards and difficulties related to the incorporation of EVs in city logistics, as outlined in a single research paper. Simultaneously addressing the potential hazards of integrating electric vehicles into SCs. The report finishes by emphasizing the need to adopt a comprehensive strategy for integrating electric vehicles into smart cities, taking into account the aforementioned challenges and opportunities. Additionally, it offers prospective future patterns to tackle these issues and facilitate the effective assimilation of EVs into intelligent urban areas.

articleTitle: Elective surgery prioritization criteria and tools: A literature review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Improving healthcare quality for patients undergoing elective surgery primarily consists of reducing waiting times to guarantee fairness and transparency. Studies on elective patient prioritization have led to the development of effective prioritization criteria and widely applicable tools. These ongoing efforts are increasingly being applied within various healthcare systems around the world. Presenting a literature review of criteria and tools for prioritizing patients in elective surgery is the aim of this article. Three databases were used to search for articles: Web of Science, PubMed and Scopus, using various keywords such as "prioritization," "elective care," "criteria," "tools," "models," and "waiting period." The search generated130 documents, of which 35 were selected. The findings demonstrate that prioritization criteria are diverse and generic. Prioritization tools use criteria by assigning weights to them. However, these tools are static and do not take into account variations in patient health while waiting for surgery. As a research perspective, we recommend the development of prioritization tools specific to patient types and pathologies, and also the inclusion of the dynamic dimension to consider changes in patients’ health during the waiting period.

articleTitle: Human factor of multi attribute decision aid making system for supply chains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Achieving optimal operation is a fundamental objective in most production and service systems. The core of this pursuit involves seeking the minimum or maximum values of one or more target functions within specific constraints. For instance, it is common to strive for the minimization of operating costs, lead times, and resource utilization, or the maximization of revenue and coverage. These objectives must be balanced against a range of factors, including market constraints, resource capacities, budgets, and technological conditions. A significant challenge in the quest for optimal operation is the quality and documentation of data. Often, data are neither clean nor well-documented, which complicates the process of finding and implementing optimal operational strategies. This paper focuses on the human element in decision-making processes, acknowledging the limitations inherent in human capabilities when making decisions. The primary aim of this paper is to present a case study that highlights the constraints of human decision-making processes. Through this case study, we examine the impact of human factors on achieving optimal operation in production and service systems. The study provides insights into how human limitations can affect the decision-making process, particularly in the context of imperfect data and the complex interplay of various operational constraints.

articleTitle: Courier, Express, Parcel market with a complex system interpretation – The Hungarian case
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The parcel delivery market functions as a complex system, according to the authors of this article. By comprehending and outlining the unique characteristics of the complex system, the authors aim to substantiate their assertion. The Covid pandemic in Hungary's Courier, Express, and Parcel market in 2020 caused a previously unprecedented increase in parcel delivery demands similarly to other countries. The epidemic-related rise in e-commerce additionally resulted significant changes to the approach by which the parcel delivery industry operated. Unexpected collaboration amongst service providers started to emerge on the parcel market in 2021. These alterations are of a kind that suggests the behavioural characteristics of a complex system. Considering that the leading service providers' autonomous operations constitute the primary characteristic of the Hungarian parcel delivery market, an analysis from a scientific perspective of the events that transpired in the Hungarian parcel delivery market is imperative to understand the reasons for this shift. Two research questions have been formulated by the authors, one of which investigates whether the parcel delivery market is considered as a system (complex system), it is conceivable for collaboration to emerge spontaneously if this is the most effective form for the system. The other research question concerns whether cooperation can be established in a market without external interference. To provide an explanation for the developments that transpired between 2020 and 2022, the authors analyse the Hungarian parcel delivery market as a complex system. In complex systems, transformation and self-organization occur naturally when the system decides that a particular shape is best for it in its current environment. During the time under review, the equilibrium of the parcel delivery market in Hungary was disrupted by the unanticipated rise in e-commerce, and the increased demands of customers nearly brought the service providers to a state of chaos. Consequently, the behaviour of service providers started to shift from their previous standards. The article's uniqueness is in its classification of the parcel delivery market as a complex system, which can be used to anticipate the current and expected behaviour of the stakeholders.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence: A Key to Smart and Sustainable Urban Freight Transport
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article delves into the functions and impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) in urban freight transport (UFT), starting by defining AI and urban freight transport as well as its performance. After citing examples of AI applications and their utilities in UFT based on a background that encompasses publications from ten years, the article examines the opportunities and challenges presented by AI in this field. Opportunities include improving route optimization, real-time monitoring, and better resource management, while challenges encompass concerns regarding data privacy, integration complexities, and ethical considerations. Ultimately, the article ends by highlighting the transformative possibilities of AI in UFT and underscores the necessity of tackling challenges to fully harness its advantages.

articleTitle: The Spiral of Managerial Innovation: Illustration through the Introduction of "Synchronous Logistics" Flow Management in a Moroccan Automotive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Managerial innovation is a determinant of organizational performance. Our article aims to go beyond the linear link between these concepts and go deeply in this relationship in order to study the virtuous spiral of managerial innovation. Using a longitudinal study of a logistics managerial innovation, the implementation of synchronous flows management, we show that it leads to an other managerial innovation in the supply chain management consisting of a new category of strategic collaboration with providers in the automotive industry in Morocco.

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling of the the one-to-one Pickup and Delivery Problem with time Windows with a single vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This paper focuses on a specific type of transportation problem known as the one-to-one Pickup and Delivery Problem with time Windows with a single vehicle (PDPTW), where the goal is to determine the next loading point for a delivery vehicle after completing a customer delivery. The objective is to minimize total transportation costs while adhering to time constraints. The article presents a mathematical formulation of the problem to facilitate its resolution and gives an overview of current methodologies and solutions through a thorough literature review. Real data from Optimalogistic, a Tunisian transport company, is used to test this strategy. The proposed approach is shown to be effective in minimizing transportation costs while adhering to time windows when the mathematical model is solved using the CPLEX solver.

articleTitle: Data Modeling Review: The case of Vaccine Lifecycle Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Vaccination is essential, particularly in light of global challenges such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Effective vaccine management is critical; however, creating a comprehensive model for seamless data integration throughout the vaccine lifecycle presents significant challenges. This paper seeks to address these challenges by highlighting the need for a model that comprehensively tackles the complex nature of the vaccine lifecycle. By evaluating existing approaches, we suggest a framework based on Data Models and Product Lifecycle Management to improve vaccine lifecycle. This study offers a thorough examination of the recent situation and explores potential directions for future studies.In summary, our study highlights the crucial role of data models in vaccine lifecycle management, which are vital tools from development to distribution. Existing models such as STEP, CPM, and IPPOP provide valuable frameworks but require adaptation to fit the highly regulated environment of vaccine lifecycle management. Our future research will focus on refining data models for Vaccine Lifecycle Management (VLM) to boost efficiency and collaboration among stakeholders, addressing the specific demands of vaccine development and management

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Transportation Marketing: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into transport service marketing, examining opportunities to enhance service quality and brand promotion within the sector. Drawing from a review of literature encompassing AI fundamentals and marketing strategies specific to transportation, this study identifies avenues for leveraging AI to optimize marketing efforts. Despite concerns surrounding AI adoption, the paper underscores the significance of careful implementation to enrich customer experiences and foster sustainable growth in the transport industry.

articleTitle: Analysis of disruptions and adaptations in the insurance supply chain in response to the COVID-19 crisis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: COVID-19 has had a significant impact on the insurance supply chain, highlighting the importance of digitalization. This health crisis has accelerated the transition to more digital insurance operations, as businesses have had to quickly adapt to the changes imposed by the pandemic. Digitalization has enabled insurers to maintain their operations, serve their customers remotely and manage requests efficiently. This shift has also paved the way for new opportunities, such as using technology to assess risk, personalize insurance policies and improve customer experience. The purpose of this article is to emphasize the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the demand for insurance services in Tunisia, particularly in relation to business interruptions. This was achieved through a survey conducted in 2021, which involved 158 insurance companies. The primary focus of this research is to assess the overall influence of COVID-19 on the insurance supply chain, with an emphasis on identifying measures that can be implemented to better prepare the insurance supply chain for similar challenges in the future. The results of the Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) affirm that the introduction of new technologies appears to be a strong priority. It also proved that digital transformation had a positive impact on customer relations and internal collaboration. Thus, it showed that digital transformation contributed to helping insurance companies better cope with the crisis.

articleTitle: Building Resilient and Sustainable Supply Chains through ESG Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The integration of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles into supply chain management is increasingly recognized as a strategic imperative for businesses facing global disruptions, environmental concerns, and regulatory pressures. This paper explores the role of ESG in enhancing supply chain resilience, sustainability, and ethical practices. It outlines the challenges companies face, such as supply chain complexities, ESG data collection, and ensuring supplier compliance. Despite these challenges, there are significant opportunities, including enhanced brand reputation, operational efficiencies, and competitive advantage, that arise from overcoming these obstacles. By adopting key ESG integration strategies companies can address vulnerabilities and build stronger supply chains. The discussion underscores the benefits of ESG integration, including attracting investment, fostering innovation, and achieving long-term sustainability, positioning it not merely as a trend but as essential for modern business success.

articleTitle: Improving operator health and safety through logistics automation in the mining sector: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Considering the significant challenges that the digital revolution must face to succeed in implementation in hazardous mining environments, an overview was presented on the history of the technological revolution in the mining industry as well as the importance of automation in mining logistics with a focus on improving the health and well-being of workers.The advancement of technology has enhanced several elements of mining operations, including safety, production, emergency response, communication, and the processing and transportation of minerals. The development of technology has been vital in preventing mining dangers and increasing mine productivity.This document summarizes the overall improvements in the mining sector over time, particularly in mining logistics, and how these advancements in technology have contributed to lower dangers and risks in workplaces.

articleTitle: The dynamic linkage between ecological footprint, foreign direct investment, industrialization, urbanization and airway freight Transportation. Evidence from BICS countries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This study investigates the interconnections between urbanization, industrialization, foreign direct investment, economic growth, freight transportation, and ecological footprint in Brazil, India, China, and South Africa. The STIRPAT model is employed to analyse their interactions during the period from 1970 to 2018. By adopting a comprehensive methodological approach, including unit root tests, lag length selection, ARDL cointegration analysis, robustness checks, and causality analyses, this study contributes to the academic discussion on ecological sustainability. The model considers air freight transportation, industrialization, foreign direct investment, economic growth, and urbanization as determinants of ecological footprint. Through these rigorous analyses, the study reveals the complex relationships among these factors and their collective impact on the environmental sustainability of the BICS nations.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Speed Advisory System for Optimal Energy Efficiency Based on Fuel Consumption and Road Speed Limit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: With the increasing number of vehicles on the road, the demand for fossil fuels continues to rise, and energy consumption and associated emissions present ongoing environmental challenges, which explains the urgent need for alternative solutions to attain sustainability in transportation. This study proposes a novel fuzzy logic (FL) based speed advisory system utilizing vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication to optimize energy efficiency in passenger vehicles. Two FL models are developed: the first estimates instantaneous fuel consumption based on vehicle speed gathered using V2I. The second calculates an adequate advisory speed considering fuel usage and road speed limits. Simulations are conducted in MATLAB and SUMO using realistic driving cycles and traffic patterns for a 17.45km route. Fuzzy Logic speed advisories are sent to vehicles via V2I to adjust their speeds accordingly. FL accurately predicts energy consumption with an estimated RMSE (Root Mean Square error) value of around 0.3%. Compared to the unequipped vehicles with Fuzzy Logic, FL advisory implementation reduces energy consumption, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CO, NOx, and particulate matter emissions by 49%, reducing the negative environmental impact. This innovative approach enables vehicles to optimize energy usage, promoting a more sustainable transportation system. In addition to reducing emissions, Fuzzy Logic speed advisories also improve air quality and minimize the adverse health effects caused by pollution. This significant environmental impact demonstrates FL's potential to enhance sustainability in transportation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Berth Allocation in the Port of Rades A Discrete Timetabling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: In this study, we will deal with a significant challenge arises in the operations along the seaside: The Berth Allocation Problem, focusing specifically on the Tunisian port of Rades. The purpose of this challenge is to guide arriving ships to free appropriate docking positions which match their characteristics in order to manage total wharf productivity. To tackle this real-world problem, we use an integer programming model. By drawing an innovative analogy not explored in the literature, connecting the berth allocation problem with university examination timetabling approaches. We shed light on the similarities, in this innovative framework, exams can be effectively treated as berths, and students can be likened to ships, where their duration of stay corresponds directly to the exam duration (timeslot). This provides a robust, conflict-free solution for one-week planning horizon, aiding the port in automatically resolving this task and boosting its productivity.

articleTitle: Cocreating Sustainability in the Circular Supply Chain: A Qualitative Exploration among Moroccan SMEs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Sustainability is a critical issue in supply chain management, with circular systems emerging as potential solutions for environmental and economic viability. However, how Moroccan Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) incorporate sustainability within circular supply chains remains underexplored.This qualitative study investigates the co-creation of sustainability among Moroccan SMEs engaged in these chains, analyzing practices, challenges, and perspectives. The methodology is based on in-depth interviews and thematic analysis, conducted using NViVO software, with a diverse sample of Moroccan SMEs from various sectors and regions.The findings reveal that these companies face difficulties such as resource constraints, limited understanding of circularity principles, and regulatory hurdles. Nonetheless, they implement innovative and collaborative strategies to promote sustainability in their circular supply chains. This research enriches the understanding of sustainability co-creation by Moroccan SMEs, highlighting the importance of collaboration, innovation, and knowledge sharing. These insights provide guidance for policymakers, industry actors, and SMEs to enhance sustainability initiatives within circular supply chains.

articleTitle: Analysis of the insurance supply chain in the context of geopolitical risks and economic uncertainty in France
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The global importance of insurance supply chains has surged in recent decades due to escalating risks, crises, wars, and uncertainties in international markets. These changes underscore the essential role of the insurance supply chain, requiring insurers to adapt in order to sustain their operations and manage risks effectively. This study investigates the impact of economic policy uncertainty and geopolitical risks on the French insurance supply chain, using annual data spanning from 1990 to 2022. We applied the Auto-Regressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to analyze both long-term and short-term relationships. The findings reveal that both geopolitical risk and economic policy uncertainty have significant and positive effects on the insurance supply chain in the short and long term, with the impact being more substantial in the long term. Additionally, the results indicate that GDP per capita significantly affects long-term insurance premiums. The reliability of these findings is corroborated through the use of Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS) and Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS) techniques.

articleTitle: Impact of the use of RFID technology in the sustainable management of the Supply Chain: case of Moroccan industrial companies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: After the COVID-19 pandemic, many companies began to understand how vulnerable and outdated their supply chain operations were. However, even before this crisis, global supply chain managers had already begun to rethink their operations in response to some fundamental changes in the behavior of not only retailers but also consumers and suppliers; Faced with a world of institutional change and increasing technological progress, companies are seeking to integrate Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and implement Sustainable Supply Chain Management (SSCM) using digital tools and techniques.; among these technologies, we deal in this paper with RFID (Radio Frequency Identification). In this sense, how does the use of RFID constitute a strategic lever in the sustainability of the supply chain? on a cross-literature review in technology and supply chain, as well as on a qualitative empirical study based on interviews processed by NVIVO and conducted with 12 companies in the industrial sector in Morocco, this article presents and discusses a set of propositions that respond to our research question.

articleTitle: Empowering Digital Supply Chains with PLM 4.0 and Emerging Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The growing industrial field, driven by digitalization and shifting market dynamics, requires that businesses adapt swiftly to meet changing demands and remain competitive. This adaptation necessitates the integration of digitalization and Industry 4.0 technologies across supply chain processes while maintaining robust product traceability. In this context, embracing product lifecycle management is currently a strategy needed for organizations seeking to achieve success in an era defined by digital transformation and increased consumer expectations. As a result, we present in this paper a comprehensive framework that integrates Product Lifecycle Management 4.0 (PLM 4.0), with a product-centric approach within the digital supply chain process. The proposed model effectively incorporates industry 4.0 technologies into every process of the supply chain while ensuring the tracking of both physical and informational product flows from inception to endof-life. As a result, the implementation of this framework improves productivity and financial outcomes, it additionally contributes to reducing environmental consequences, aligning with global sustainability goals. Furthermore, it offers valuable perspectives and actionable recommendations for professionals, scholars, and policymakers engaged in supply chain management and the ongoing process of digital transformation.

articleTitle: Where are you going, logistics of the future? : (Quo vadis logistica futuri?)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The current economic context, the increasing complexity of logistics systems and processes and the increasing unpredictability of the business environment in which enterprises operate require a new look at expectations towards logistics. In the light of the importance of theory in scientific research, the key research problem in this article, which is controversial in its theoretical dimension, is to determine potential directions of changes in thinking about future logistics in the context of its transposition from the current state. This goal will be achieved through a systematic review of the literature, deductively leading to an attempt to systematize the dimensions and optics of perception of contemporary logistics. The research process also used the results of surveys, which had a monomodal inquiry character, allowing for the identification of the opinions of Gen Z respondents in relation to the image of the future image of logistics. The adopted methodological approach forced the need to reflect on the future of the perception of the concept of logistics, especially since the world is no longer only physical, but cyberphysical. Finally, an original formulation of the future framework for perceiving logistics took place and a revised definition of the future supply chain was established by taking into account various main challenges, highlighting new elements of flow, both in the cyber and physical world. Finally, a future research.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Human Capital: Pillar of Supply Chain Resilience
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Today, the true strength of companies lies in their ability to enhance their human capital, thereby nourishing the resilience of their supply chain against market challenges and fluctuations. The primary objective of this study is to analyze how the enhancement of human capital plays a decisive role in the robustness and resilience of logistics chains. We have observed the correlation between these two aspects, and the findings have been confirmed by human resource managers and logistics professionals. This study aims to provide valuable insights on how improving human capital can be a key driver of operational resilience in the supply chain while highlighting the importance of collaboration between HR and logistics departments to ensure lasting success.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Agility in the Supply Chain of Large Moroccan Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Looking at the agility of supply chains raises the question of how agility helps to explain how supply chains survive adversity and thrive against the odds. As a first step, it seems appropriate to take stock of supply chain agility, beginning with an exploration of distinctive characteristics of supply chain organizational structures to highlight the complexity of intra- and inter-organizational relationships. However, the seamless coordination of activities within and between organizations can lead to the creation of a collaborative network and a flexible, adaptable and non-rigid structure, which contributes to a better overall agility and responsiveness of the supply chain system. Thus, the challenges of strengthening supply chain agility are outlined through an analysis of the concept's dimensions.The aim of this article is to understand and analyze how and under what conditions the introduction of artificial intelligence in Moroccan companies has the potential to boost the agility of supply chains. For this purpose, a theoretical framework for analyzing our research problem will be provided, enabling the construction of a logical, coherent and comprehensible research model. A qualitative study will then be carried out to qualitatively test our research model. Our aim is to demonstrate that it is not enough to implement a variety of software packages to enhace the agility of supply chains, but that the organizational and human factors also need to be reviewed.

articleTitle: Current trends in scientific research on managerial innovations in healthcare supply chain: A bibliometric analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article is designed to highlight trends in managerial innovation in the healthcare supply chain, while attempting to analyse recent publications. The importance of this research extends both to the academic world and to practical applications through the prospects of a future that always remains unpredictable and whose projections are doomed to be often undone by innovation initiatives. The study therefore required bibliometric analysis using two software packages: Dimensions, which identified 90 relevant publications from 2015 to 2024. Secondly, Vosviewer was used to analyse prolific authors, eminent journals, contributing countries and influential publications.

articleTitle: Regional transport disparities in Tunisia : Development of a Social Transport Sustainability Index STSI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: the aim of this study is to establish a Social Transport Sustainability Index (STSI) with a view to highlighting the regional disparities in Tunisia in terms of transport. First, a set of socially relevant indicators of transport sustainability was collected and organised describing the Tunisian cities, then the indicators were normalised using the max min method, followed by the principal component analysis (PCA) method to weight the indicators and to combine them into sub-dimension indices. Finally, these sub-dimensions indices were weighted and aggregated to form the composite index specific to the social dimension of transport sustainability for each Tunisian city. The results showed that the governorates of Tunis (0.784), Ariana (0.737), Ben Arous (0.693), Manouba (0.659), Sousse (0.658) and Monastir (0.603) are the most socially sustainable in terms of transport, while the governorates of Tozeur (0. 161), Kasserine (0.194), Siliana (0.257), Le Kef (0.265), Sidi Bouzid (0.266) and Kairouan (0.295) are the least socially sustainable cities with regard to transport.

articleTitle: The Multidimensional Impact of Information System Integration on SCM : Evidence from Citrus Packing Stations in Morocco
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This study delves into the pivotal role of Information System (IS) integration in enhancing Supply Chain Management (SCM) within the Citrus Packing Stations established in Morocco, a critical component of the national agricultural sector. Amidst climatic challenges and the need for market competitiveness, this research addresses the significant gap in understanding how IS adoption influences SCM effectiveness, both directly and indirectly. Employing a mixed-methods framework, this study synthesizes qualitative insights and quantitative analyses to validate a comprehensive research model that evaluates IS integration's influence across seven key SCM dimensions: product quality, operational cost reduction, delivery timeliness, inventory management, customer satisfaction, supply chain visibility, and overall SCM effectiveness. The findings reveal significant predictive relationships between IS integration and SCM enhancement, highlighting the transformative potential of technology in optimizing supply chain operations within Morocco's citrus sector. Despite its focused scope on the citrus industry, the study acknowledges its limitations and suggests broader exploratory research to generalize findings across diverse agricultural domains. Additionally, it underscores the potential of emerging technologies like machine learning and advanced analytics to further revolutionize SCM practices. This research offers valuable insights for both scholars and practitioners aiming to leverage technology for supply chain optimization, thereby supporting economic growth and sustainability in agriculture.

articleTitle: Logistics Service Provider: Literature review, perspectives, and opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The supply chain is a complex network involving entities managing the flow of products, services, finances, and information from source to customer. This structure is segmented into three levels: Direct, Extended, and Global, with the logistics service provider (LSP) emerging as a key participant at the Global Level. LSPs, as intermediaries, coordinate supply chain organizations, managing logistics activities and resources. Industrial enterprises often outsource their logistics operations to LSPs, leading to the transfer of equipment and personnel. LSPs are classified into five types: 1PL to 5PL, each specializing in different logistics functions. 1PL handles transportation, 2PL includes warehousing management, and 3PL extends to various logistics activities like transport, storage, and consulting. 4PL acts as consultants to optimize logistics, and 5PL focuses on integrated logistics services within supply chain management. This article aims to review systematic reviews on the role of LSPs, analyzing current trends and future perspectives. A comprehensive search identified 849 articles, narrowed down to 22 relevant ones published between 2010 and 2023. After thorough analysis and elimination of duplicates, 6 articles were selected. Additional research yielded 12 supplementary articles, resulting in a final compilation of 18 articles. This systematic approach ensures a diverse representation of sources for a robust examination of LSPs

articleTitle: Exploration of the perception and level of integration of Supply chain resilience criteria in Moroccan companies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article analyzes how Moroccans companies’ percept and integrate supply chain resilience (SCR) principles. As supply chain are increasingly exposed to disruptions, especially in the period of the COVID-19- pandemic, it is crucial to comprehend the extent to which Moroccan companies incorporate these principles into their operational strategy. Drawing from a literature review and empirical data, the study focus on two research questions: What is the perception and understanding of Moroccan companies regarding SCR? To what extent do Moroccan companies integrate SCR principles into their operational strategy? The findings provide valuable insights to assist Moroccan companies in enhancing their resilience to supply chain disruptions.

articleTitle: Decidated bus lanes and the attractiveness of public transport
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: We examine the effects of the improvement of public transport based on dedicated bus lanes, optimized (i) frequencies and (ii) spacing between the stations. We find that dedicated bus lanes yield the most important impacts when congestion is high, which is the case in most metropolitan areas. Our analysis is based on micro-simulation and produces a complete spatial accounting of traffic flows, the levels of emissions greenhouse gases and fine particulates.

articleTitle: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Supply Chain Resilience: bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The escalating complexity of dynamic supply chain processes necessitates adaptive technology. Although various AI- based supply chain applications have emerged recently, there has been limited focus on utilizing artificial intelligence specifically within supply chain functionsHarnessing artificial intelligence provides notable benefits, mainly by significantly enhancing supply chain resilience. Given the limited existing research, this research explores current artificial intelligence applications within supply chain processes and pinpoints areas for additional exploration investigation. We conducted a review of 80 research articles published during the period from 2020 and 2023 retrieved from the Scopus databaseOur analysis outlines critical features regarding artificial intelligence's role in improving supply chain resilience. Ultimately, we assert that judicious utilization of AI across diverse supply chain processes facilitates the development of a resilient supply chain, underpinning a robust decision support system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Supply Chain Resilience and Sustainability through Robustness and Agility Attributes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Increasing sustainability regulations compel businesses to rethink their economic, environmental, and social approaches. The possibility of supply chain disruption, whether natural or human-induced, presents a significant challenge for managers. Therefore, it becomes crucial to design a flexible and robust logistics network to anticipate, manage, and sustain performance in the face of these disruptions. Therefore, the study of robustness and agility influence on SC sustainability and resilience will be the objective of this work. By exploring these fundamental concepts following a literature review, the relationships between these concepts and the effects of robustness and agility on sustainability and resilience were studied using the QFD method. The results identified that attributes with the strongest impact for robustness are avoidance, visibility, and resistance, and for agility are market knowledge, internal integration, and flexibility of the logistics chain. In conclusion, this work sheds light on the importance of designing robust and agile logistics strategies to meet resilience and sustainability needs, highlighting key attributes to strengthen the supply chain in a complex and changing world.

articleTitle: Demand-Driven Supply Chain Harmonizing Digitalization, Resilience, and Sustainability : Exploring the Synergy through a Bibliometric Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: As businesses emerge in response to dynamic markets, the imperative to assess alternative approaches becomes preeminent in order to effectively meet the challenging demands of the current evolving supply chain environment. The real-time visibility into demand and supply levels enables unparalleled supply-chain performance, consequently, the adoption of Demand-Driven Supply Chain (DDSC) practices has been increased over the past decade. This adoption is particularly prominent to enhance supply chain efficiency in the face of changing market conditions and fluctuations in customer needs.This paper defines the concept of DDSC, illuminating its core benefits, and exploring its intersection with the critical pillars of contemporary supply chain management, namely digitalization, resilience, and sustainability.

articleTitle: Hospital logistics based on blockchain: A literature review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The objective of the document is to offer a comprehensive perspective on blockchain technology and its potential to transform hospital logistics. In this l literature review, we will l first describe the main concerns of hospital logistics. Then, we will emphasize the importance of blockchain technology in healthcare suppl y chain management t. To address this, we will conduct a literature review, analyzing articles and publications from data bases such as Science Direct, Scopus, Cairn, Google Scholar, and PubMed. focusing directly on blockchain and hospital supply chain. The results reveal that blockchain technology is a crucial and effective element in hospital supply chains. It ensures better traceability, relevant data storage, and efficient real-time product tracking, thus enhancing hospital logistics performance. In the healthcare sector, blockchain provides data origin, supports real need in healthcare sector demands, and ensures the immutability of transactions occurring in multiple directions. Furthermore, blockchain is still in its early stages in healthcare system, particularly in hospital supply chain.

articleTitle: Multilayer perception neural networks method-based supply chain performance prediction by a new augmented of SCOR® metrics: SCOR®4.0
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The Supply Council Operations Reference (SCOR<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>) is an industry standard model used to define supply activities in operations management. In order to forecast supply chain performance, this study suggests a novel SCOR4.0 model that combines artificial neural networks and SCOR<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> metrics. The three-level hierarchical structure of the model allows it to handle multi-criteria decision-making issues. Statistical hypothesis testing and random subsampling cross-validation show how much more accurate the model is at making predictions. By using a prospective diagnosis of supply chain performance, the suggested approach facilitates rational decision-making and offers benefits like increased accuracy and the capacity to assist decision-making in a globalizing world.

articleTitle: The Role of Reusable Packaging in Supply Chain Management: Insights from Machinery, Aerospace, and Automotive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Amidst global supply chain disruptions and stricter sustainability standards, this study examines the role of reusable transit packaging in enhancing supply chain efficiency and sustainability, particularly in the US aerospace, automotive, and machinery industries. The study explores the current adoption and perception of reusable packaging in these key sectors by employing a multifaceted methodology that includes a comprehensive survey, semi-structured interviews with industry professionals, and a literature review. Results indicate a growing recognition of the benefits of reusable packaging but reveal a series of significant barriers, such as regulatory gaps and high implementation costs. The discussion section summarizes the key findings, identifies the primary barriers hindering the broader implementation of reusable packaging, and outlines the subsequent steps in crafting a functional framework. This framework will be designed to assist organizations in advocating for policy support. It will be done by prioritizing these mechanisms according to their potential business impact and the practicality of their implementation.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Supply Chain Management : Implications for the Smart Cities of Tomorrow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
